articles.title_orig: Israel election: Exit polls suggest no clear winner with Eisenkot's bloc neck and neck with Netanyahu
articles.title_zh: Israel election: Exit polls suggest no clear winner with Eisenkot's bloc neck and neck with Netanyahu
articles.content_orig:
Israel's election result is too close to call , with Gadi Eisenkot's bloc neck and neck with Benjamin Natanyahu's camp in two exit polls; a third puts the PM's camp marginally ahead - both have fallen short of a majority
Eisenkot leads the newly formed Yashar party and is the main figure in the "change bloc", a group of opposition parties with the shared goal of ousting  Netanyahu
The exit polls also suggest Netanyahu's Likud party is set to be the biggest single party in the Israeli parliament
Netanyahu says a "strong" right-wing government must be formed, while Eisenkot tells supporters that Israel voted to end Netanyahu's term
Official results started being released from midnight local time (22:00 GMT), but counting could take days
What lies ahead is likely to be weeks or months of protracted negotiations between the parties, with numerous options on the table, our reporter in Tel Aviv writes
All 120 seats in the Knesset, Israel's parliament, are up for grabs, but no party has ever won a majority and in the past governments have been made up of coalitions
Edited by Chris Graham, with James Landale, Hugo Bachega and Tom Bennett in Israel
We are pausing our live coverage now. Here is what we know so far:
You can catch up on all the latest developments in our news story here .
Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main rival, celebrates at his party's headquarters
Supporters of Netanyahu's party Likud arrive at the headquarters
Cheering supporters at the Joint List alliance of Arab parties
Tel Aviv celebrations shortly after the exit polls were revealed
Far-right Otzma Yehudit party leader Itamar Ben Gvir (C), who was in Netanyahu's coalition, addresses his supporters at the election night rally
Trump hung over the election, with some of Netanyahu's supporters brandishing signs depicting the US President
Netanyahu strikes a defiant tone as he addresses his supporters early on Wednesday morning
Before concluding his speech, Netanyahu tells his supporters that Israel has a "unique opportunity" alongside President Donald Trump to "remove the Iranian threat once and for all".
Israel and the US launched joint strikes on Iran in 2025 targeting nuclear facilities, and jointly struck Iran in February beginning the current ongoing conflict.
Commentators say it is unlikely that either a Netanyahu or Eisenkot-led bloc would change the current course of Israel's involvement in the Iran war.
Netanyahu speaks at the Likud rally
Netanyahu says the current results show it is too early to call, saying he is waiting for "real results" before an outcome can be decided.
Current projections show his bloc tied with the bloc led by his main rival Gadi Eisenkot.
He says Israel cannot be led by a government held up with "Arab backing".
The Arab parties are on track to win a record number of seats, with both major blocs falling short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Israeli parliament.
Benjamin Netanyahu is speaking at his election rally where supporters of his Likud party have gathered.
"Likud is the largest party," he says to a cheering crowd.
"We must establish a strong right-wing national government."
While current polls show Likud has won the most seats out of any party, it still falls far short of a majority needed to form a government.
The bloc led by Netanyahu and the bloc led by opposition parties are currently tied, according to revised exit polls from two of Israel's  broadcasters, while a third has put Netanyahu marginally ahead.
No party has ever won an outright majority, which means a coalition government has always been formed.
This process begins after the votes have been counted and Israel's president will consult with party leaders, and then invite whichever leader he believes has the best chance of forming a government.
That candidate then has 28 days to form a coalition, although they can request a 14-day extension if extra time is needed.
If negotiations fail within this period, the president can choose another candidate to try to form their own coalition.
If that also fails, Knesset members can ask the president to allow a third leader to try. And if that's unsuccessful, new elections will be called.
Between 2019 and 2022, Israel held five separate elections as parties struggled time and again to co-operate.
Following the 2022 elections, Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the biggest party, winning 32 of the 120 seats. He later formed a coalition with several far-right parties, which gave him and his allies a majority of 64 seats.
New exit poll show a tie between Netanyahu and Eisenkot's blocs.
Israel's Kan 11 and Channel 13 news networks have published updates to their exit polls showing the two rival blocs projected to win 51 seats each.
Channel 12 has also revised its exit poll showing the Eisenkot-led bloc marginally behind on 50, while placing Netanyahu's bloc on 52. Earlier, they showed the anti-Netanyahu bloc slightly ahead of the incumbent prime minister.
The winning bloc needs at least 61 seats in the Knesset to form a majority government.
Official results are starting to trickle through from Israel's Central Electoral Committee with 2.5% of votes counted.
Gabriela Pomeroy Live reporter
Exit polls show record gains and turnout for the Arab parties.
I spoke to one of the activists who campaigned to get out the Arab vote  - 29-year-old Mahdi Kabaha, a lawyer in the mainly Arab northern town of Umm Al-Fahm.
"This is a historic night. Arab society showed up and said it clearly: we are here, and we are part of the decision," he says.
Arab voters make up about a fifth of the Israeli electorate and just over half voted in the last election. Many have been reluctant to vote in the past as they âdonât want to legitimise Israeli institutions," Kabaha says.
He has been promoting voting among the Arab community in order to remove far-right ministers like Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.
One of the biggest issues for Arab voters is crime in Arab areas and a lack of policing.
Kabaha campaigned for Israeli Arabs to come out and vote, telling them they should use their voting power to shape the government. âThere is a big difference between [left-leaning Democrats leader] Yair Golan and Ben Gvir in the government. One wants to
take more land and expel Palestinians, and the other wants to find a solution for
two people,â he adds.
Tom Bennett Reporting from Eisenkot's watch party
Eisenkot addresses supporters at Yashar's party headquarters.
Gadi Eisenkot has just arrived at his partyâs HQ here in Tel Aviv, taking a long walk through the crowd onto stage, surrounded by the candidates from his Yashar Party.
âWe made history,â he says. âThis morning, the people of Israel went to a referendum on the leadership of the coming years. The public decided in favour of change.
"The Israeli public voted against the continuation of Netanyahu's term," he says, to big cheers from the crowd.
âIn an election with such high voter turnout, it would be a mistake to go to additional elections. It is our duty, and my personal responsibility, to do everything to respect the will of the people.â
The national anthem was then played before he took an Israeli flag from the crowd and waved it, before exiting the stage.
The official vote count is starting to come through.
So far 2,670 votes have been tallied, according to Israel's Central Elections Committee. That represents almost 0.1% of the total number of votes.
Since the polling stations closed at 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT), reporting has relied on exit poll data â which is not an official count, but rather surveys of voters exiting polling stations conducted by media companies.
While the official tally so far is not a meaningful sample size, it does show the electoral body is starting to report as expected.
The turnout for this year's Israeli general election was 77.7% as of 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT) when polls closed, the country's Central Election Committee has said.
The figure represents 5,695,6

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu, Eisenkot blocs running close, but both shy of majority
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu, Eisenkot blocs running close, but both shy of majority
articles.content_orig:
The outcome of Israel's election hung in the balance as of Wednesday, with both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and challenger Gadi Eisenkot appearing to be well off the numbers needed to form a governing coalition.
An updated Channel 13 poll early Wednesday put both blocs at 51 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, the Times of Israel reported. A coalition needs 61 to be able to govern. Channel 12 and Kan 11 showed Eisenkot's bloc slightly ahead at 52-50. Arab-led parties, which belong to neither camp, were projected at 17 to 18 seats, their strongest showing ever.
Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff, declared victory and said the preliminary results should give him the first right to try to form a government. "The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and his October 7 government," he said in a statement on X .
Exit polls are not the official results, which are formally published a week after the election, on Nov. ​4. Around 77.7% of eligible voters turned out to cast their ballots, the highest in a Knesset election in 27 years , according to the Central Elections Committee.
The vote came as Israel's first national election since Hamas's Oct. 7, 2023 attack and the subsequent wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, and was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's dominance of Israeli politics since 2009.
Netanyahu's supporters credit him with steering Israel through the war and standing up to international pressure, while critics point to his long-running corruption trial, controversial judicial overhaul efforts, and handling of the Gaza war as evidence that he is unfit for office. Netanyahu faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over the Gaza campaign, which he has rejected.
The historic Arab-party result is a factor to watch in coalition talks. Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas said that "our vote will change the government." Joint List faction chairman Ahmad Tibi had previously outlined a plan to prevent Netanyahu from remaining in power after the elections, according to the Jerusalem Post .
The pro-Palestinian stance of Arab-led parties aligns them more closely with Eisenkot than with Netanyahu, said Amin Saikal, an adjunct senior fellow at Singapore's S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, though neither man has said he would embrace them.
"Even if Eisenkot's alliance wins more seats, it's less likely to be able to form a governing majority without including Arab and left-wing parties," said Michael Feller, chief strategist at Geopolitical Strategy. "The next government's policies on Iran, Palestine and security may otherwise stay the same."
However, Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman, whose party is projected at seven to nine seats and is currently in the opposition bloc with Eisenkot, refused during the campaign to rely on Arab parties.
Earlier on Tuesday, Netanyahu and his far-right coalition partners warned of strong Arab participation in the vote, drawing accusations of racism from opponents.
"If we don't wake up now, we'll find ourselves with ​a government of Mansour Abbas and Ahmed Tibi," he said , after a series of posts highlighting long queues at polling stations in Arab communities.
Even if Eisenkot ends up with more seats, Netanyahu may use the upcoming weeks or months to his advantage by seeking to stall the formation of the new government, said Amin Saikal, an adjunct senior fellow at Singapore's S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies.
The prime minister will "fight for his political survival," Saikal said.

articles.title_orig: Opinion | Manila speaks with 2 voices on China
articles.title_zh: Opinion | Manila speaks with 2 voices on China
articles.content_orig:
Conflicting statements from the Philippines’ diplomatic and security arms add uncertainty to an already fraught relationship with Beijing
Manila sent two strikingly different messages to Beijing on October 13. At the Malacanang Palace, a presidential spokeswoman reaffirmed Manila’s commitment to sustaining diplomatic and economic ties with China, saying “China needs the Philippines, and the Philippines needs China”.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jnr has defended the contrasting messages over China. He argues there is no contradiction between them, insisting that the diplomatic and defence arms of his administration are working towards the same objective through different approaches.

articles.title_orig: How China’s ancient capital staked a claim to the nation’s fastest export growth
articles.title_zh: How China’s ancient capital staked a claim to the nation’s fastest export growth
articles.content_orig:
Exports jumped 142.1 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, with computing equipment and integrated circuits making up more than 76 per cent
A booming semiconductor industry is helping drive a surge in trade in Xian, one of China’s ancient capitals, making it the country’s top performer by trade growth among provincial capitals and provincial-level cities for which data is publicly available.
The capital of western China’s Shaanxi province recorded a 115.5 per cent year-on-year surge in trade during the first nine months of 2026. Exports far outpaced imports, climbing 142.1 per cent.
Two product categories drove much of that export growth. Shipments of automatic data processing equipment and parts jumped 388.1 per cent year on year, while integrated circuits rose 251 per cent. Taken together, these categories accounted for 76.5 per cent of total exports.

articles.title_orig: Israel Election 2026 live updates: Netanyahu, Eisenkot caught in deadlock
articles.title_zh: Israel Election 2026 live updates: Netanyahu, Eisenkot caught in deadlock
articles.content_orig:
Fox News Digital speaks with three experts on Israel’s high-stakes election and the fight over Netanyahu’s political future. The election is set for Oct. 27, 2026.
JERUSALEM — Israel’s high-stakes election on Oct. 27 pits the longest serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, against the highly decorated retired Lt. Gen. Gadi Eisenkot. While fairly new to politics, Eisenkot has an impressive resume that could help him become the Jewish state's next leader.
According to a number of polls, Eisenkot's centrist political party, Yashar, has a narrow lead over Netanyahu's Likud. To form a government, Yashar or Likud will need to cobble together a 61-seat majority of parties to be able to form a new coalition government.
TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, speaks from behind a podium with a banner reading "Yashar with Eisenkot" during an event presenting the party's full candidate list ahead of October's general election on Sept. 7, 2026 in Rosh HaAyin, Israel. Eisenkot, a retired chief of the Israel Defense Forces, has emerged as the foremost challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. (Erik Marmor/Getty Images)
He was born in Tiberias in Israel’s north to a Jewish-Moroccan family who relocated to Israel’s southernmost city, Eilat, on the Red Sea when he was a toddler.
A career soldier, he opted to serve in the infantry. He was part of the elite Golani Brigade and reached the zenith of the military with his 2015 appointment to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) chief of staff in 2015 until 2019.
Yossi Melman, one of Israel’s most respected journalists on intelligence and defense reporting, told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot, "Is 100% a soldier. He is very brave and humble. He is an officer and gentleman."
Melman noted that when Eisenkot was chosen to be the next IDF chief of staff, he declined because he felt that then General Benny Gantz should receive the appointment. Melman asked, "How many people would do that? He was selected after Gantz. It shows his traits of modesty, honesty and not arrogant."
Melman said, "It is a miracle he is leading in the polls. He is the antithesis of a what a politician should be. He is not a great orator when you compare him to Netanyahu. He radiates honesty."
BENJAMIN NETANYAHU'S LEGACY AND POLITICAL FUTURE ON THE LINE IN ISRAEL'S OCT 27 ELECTION
Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot attends the Jerusalem Residents Conference on Aug. 12, 2026 in Jerusalem. Gadi Eisenkot, a retired chief of the Israel Defense Forces and current leader of the Yashar party, has emerged as the foremost challenger to Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of October's general election. (Erik Marmor/Getty Images)
Eisenkot’s Mizrahi background — Jews who originate from North Africa and the Middle East — would mean, if he prevails, that he would be the first Israeli Prime Minister of Moroccan origin. The Prime Minister’s office has been held by Israelis of Eastern European descent (Ashkenazi) since the rebirth of the Jewish state in 1948.
After Hamas invaded Israel on Oct. 7, 2023 and slaughtered over 1,200 people, including more than 40 Americans, Eisenkot joined Netanyahu’s war cabinet as a minister without portfolio.
Melman said Eisenkot "did not set any political conditions" and "his presence in the cabinet saved Netanyahu." After eight months of serving in the war cabinet, Eisenkot resigned, blaming the prime minister for failing to implement a comprehensive strategy.
The war against the Iran-backed terrorist movement Hamas took an enormous toll on the battle-hardened General Eisenkot and his family. Hamas killed his son, 25-year-old Master Sergeant Gal Eisenkot, in Dec. 2023. The terrorist organization also killed two nephews of Eisenkot. Netanyahu and his wife Sara said at the time that they were devastated by Gal’s death and Eisenkot was a "true hero."
ZIONISM EXPLAINED FROM ITS BIBLICAL ORIGINS TO THE REBIRTH OF THE STATE OF ISRAEL
Gadi Eisenkot, former Israeli army chief of staff and head of the Yashar party, is seen at the Black Arrow memorial site near Kibbutz Mefalsim during a visit to deliver a statement near the border with the Gaza Strip on Oct. 15, 2026, ahead of the Israel's legislative election. (Ilia Yefimovich/AFP via Getty Images)
Danny Orbach, a military historian from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, gave his take on the leading contender to replace Netanyahu. "I think his military record and his prospects as a national leader have both significant strengths and serious weaknesses. He bears considerable responsibility for shaping the IDF that existed on Oct. 7, 2023. And that was, paradoxically, both the army that proved capable of defeating Hezbollah, striking Iran and achieving unprecedented military successes in the extraordinarily difficult, tunnel-ridden battlefield of Gaza and the army that failed so miserably on Oct. 7."
He continued that, "Like other chiefs of staff, Eisenkot bears responsibility for the decisions that reduced the army's size and for the infamous ‘conceptzia’ [Hebrew word for concept] regarding Hamas. In that respect, I consider him just as culpable as Netanyahu."
Israel’s military, intelligence and political establishments bought into the ‘conceptzia’ that Hamas could be housebroken with massive infusions of economic aid. Hamas, however, was wedded to its radical Islamist ideology —the destruction of the Jewish state — and used the funds to advance its war aims.
Orbach noted that "I don't think most of Eisenkot's support stems from his energy, enthusiasm or even his political platform. My impression is that Eisenkot has emerged as the default ‘non-Bibi’ candidate, the politician who currently channels much of the camp's hopes and expectations."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Israeli Chief of Staff Gadi Eizenkot (L) give a press conference in Tel Aviv, on Dec. 4, 2018. Israel's army said today it has discovered Hezbollah tunnels infiltrating its territory from Lebanon and launched an operation to destroy them, a move likely to raise tensions with the Iran-backed group. (Jack Guez/AFP Via Getty Images)
Orbach added that "I also doubt that Eisenkot would have had the political determination to stand up to the Biden administration on such matters."
Netanyahu and former President Biden repeatedly clashed over Biden’s attempts to rope in Israel’s efforts to defeat Iran’s seven-front war against the Jewish state.
The military historian, however, noted that "I believe an Eisenkot government could address several of Israel's most urgent problems. It would remove Ben Gvir from power, confront the growing problem of Jewish extremist violence and terrorism in the West Bank, and begin repairing Israel's severely damaged international legitimacy."
Itamar Ben-Gvir is a controversial right-wing firebrand politician and the current minister of national security since 2022, who has outraged many Western European and foreign leaders with his heated rhetoric against the Palestinians.
TIMELINE OF DECADES-LONG ISRAELI-ARAB, PALESTINIAN CONFLICT
Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot attends the funeral for his son, First Sergeant Major Gal Meir Eisenkot, 25 years old, at the Herzliya cemetery on Dec. 8, 2023 in Herzliya, Israel. The Israel Defense Forces said the 25-year-old major, son of the cabinet minister and former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, died on Thursday in Gaza. (Dima Vazinovich / Middle East Images / Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images))
Eisenkot’s wife, Hannah, comes from an American Jewish family. U.S. General Joseph Dunford awarded Eisenkot the Commander of the Legion of Merit because of his "exceptionally meritorious service as chief of the General Staff of the IDF" and his "contribution to the strategic cooperation between the United States and Israel [that] will have a lasting effect on both countries," according to the Washington Institute, where Eisenkot served as a military fellow in 2019

articles.title_orig: ‘Awfully bleak’: why global carmakers keep losing ground in China’s vast market
articles.title_zh: ‘Awfully bleak’: why global carmakers keep losing ground in China’s vast market
articles.content_orig:
Carmakers are scrambling to revamp their strategies as China’s cash-strapped consumers turn away from expensive foreign brands
Global carmakers are searching for a way to survive in China’s cutthroat market, as they continue to lose ground to domestic competitors in a landscape that is increasingly tilting towards electric vehicles.
International auto brands from Volkswagen to Toyota saw their market share in the Chinese mainland slide once again in the third quarter of the year, as consumers turned away from expensive foreign cars amid an economic slowdown and the Iran war.
Foreign marques accounted for less than 30 per cent of deliveries over the period, down from 34.6 per cent a year earlier, as they delivered just 1.38 million cars to mainland customers, according to data from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA).

articles.title_orig: They bought cabins to live on a luxury cruise ship. High fuel costs got them kicked off in Cambodia.
articles.title_zh: They bought cabins to live on a luxury cruise ship. High fuel costs got them kicked off in Cambodia.
articles.content_orig:
A residential cruise ship halted operations in Cambodia on Tuesday amid soaring fuel costs , leaving passengers in limbo after the U.S. company that operates it ordered them to disembark.
Florida-based Villa Vie Residences said in a news release that it was working to identify “temporary living arrangements” for people aboard The Odyssey, a 642-foot cruise ship that launched from Belfast, Northern Ireland, three years ago and promised passengers “an unparalleled lifestyle of luxury and exploration” as it toured the planet.
Cabins on The Odyssey were for sale or rent.
According to the company , the ship can accommodate 650 residents; it isn’t clear how many were on board Tuesday or where in Cambodia they disembarked.
An executive with the company, Mikael Petterson, declined to provide additional details in an email to NBC News. In a release this year announcing the company’s second residential cruise ship, Petterson said The Odyssey was 85% sold.
The company said in Tuesday’s release that it had taken significant measures to reduce fuel consumption but that those steps had failed to offset the spike in costs.
Global oil prices have surged since the war with Iran began this year, disrupting the world’s flow of fuel. Oil prices climbed to their highest levels since this spring this month.
“Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution,” the company said. “Our focus now is on supporting residents, crew, and employees while we work toward restructuring and recapitalization over the next 60 days. That work is ongoing, and no outcome is assured.”
Randy Cassingham, a resident on the boat, wrote in a blog post that he learned his journey was over after a company official posted a note on a message board for the ship shortly after 7 a.m. Monday.
The Odyssey was entering a “temporary lay up” period — indicating it would no longer be used — and everyone had to disembark by 2 p.m., the message said, according to Cassingham, who runs ResidentialCruising.com and didn’t immediately reply to an interview request.
Cassingham attributed the development to a “cascade of problems” that he would detail later.
Pamela Reckamp, who rented a cabin with her husband and disembarked this month, said in an interview that she wasn’t surprised that the ship’s journey was over.
Reckamp, 59, recalled having attended a meeting in early September at which a company official asked cabin owners to help them raise $1 million so they could leave Ha Long Bay, Vietnam.
“She said, ‘If we don’t get this money, we have about four days of the ship running,’” Reckamp recalled. “‘Then the lights will go off and the AC will go off.’”
When the ship’s financial issues were raised during another meeting a few weeks later, Reckamp recalled, a woman stood up and said she’d bought a cabin in August and hadn’t been made aware of the issues.
“I sold my house,” Reckamp recalled the woman saying. “I sold my car. I bought my home on this ship.”
Reckamp said she felt terrible for the residents and the staff, who she said were lovely.
“We dodged a bullet,” she added.
Villa Vie Residences didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday night.
In a lawsuit filed last year, a company that bought a cabin on The Odyssey for $469,000 accused Villa Vie Residences of fraud, alleging it misrepresented its financial stability.
The company’s business model was not financially sound, the suit alleges, “but rather precarious.”
The plaintiffs are asking for a jury trial and unspecified damages of more than $100,000. Villa Vie Residences denied the allegations in the suit, which is ongoing.
Other cabins on the ship were available for significantly less money. Even though 85% of the ship was sold, the company said in 2024, prospective residents could still “secure their dream home starting at just $119,000.”
“When we launched Odyssey, we set out to prove that residential cruising wasn’t just possible — it was sustainable,” Petterson said in July.
Tim Stelloh is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.

articles.title_orig: Ex-JPMorgan banker in 'sex slave' suit accused of getting sister to lie about kissing, racial remark: filing
articles.title_zh: Ex-JPMorgan banker in 'sex slave' suit accused of getting sister to lie about kissing, racial remark: filing
articles.content_orig:
The ex-JPMorgan banker who accused his boss of making him her “sex slave” got his sister to lie in sworn testimony for him — claiming she saw the boss kiss her bro on the neck and tell him, “I own you, Brownie” — according to a new filing from the bank that seeks to dismiss the case.
Chirayu Rana allegedly enlisted the help of both his sis and a close friend to back his lurid allegations against Lorna Hajdini — who fired back last month that Rana was actually waging a “deliberate and sustained scheme” to portray her as a racist sexual predator and criminal.
In a Monday night filing in Manhattan federal court, JPMorgan renewed its allegations of lies and misconduct by Rana, saying they deserve “the most serious sanction available.”
The bank said the money man got his sister Chandani Rana and chum Allan Flott to lie in order to bolster his accusations that Hajdini forced him to have sex and demanded submissive behavior in general.
Chandani Rana initially swore to seeing Hajdini kiss her sibling on the neck and saying denigrating words along the lines of,  “I own you, Brownie” — echoing her brother’s allegations of racism.
Chandani Rana took back the remarks earlier this month, saying:  “I have never seen Ms. Hajdini engage in any inappropriate, sexual, harassing, threatening, or intoxicated conduct toward my brother or anyone else.”
Flott previously claimed Hajdini exhorted her to join Chirayu Rana for a threesome in a bedroom at Flott’s place, allegedly saying, “You know, I own Chirayu, so you’d better come join.” JPMorgan said Flott was “led astray” by his friend, though he’s yet to take back the story.
Back in April, Rana accused Hajdini of coercing him into sex and promising career advances in return – including forcing him into oral sex, grabbing his genitals, and threatening to “ruin” him if he didn’t obey.  He also accused the company for racism and creating an environment for sexual harassment.
JPMorgan and Hajdini — who countersued in May, saying the accusations torched her career and damaged her reputation — are demanding Chirayu Rana cover their legal costs.
“No order can fully restore Ms. Hajdini’s reputation ​or undo what she has suffered,” her lawyer Melissa Rodriguez said in a court filing. “But the court can put an end to this fraudulent litigation, hold ​those responsible accountable, and put an end to Ms. Hajdini’s ongoing nightmare.”
Rana has had trouble getting legal representation throughout the case.
His latest lawyer, Jon Norinsberg, has asked to leave the case, pointing to “irreconcilable differences” with Rana. Norinsberg declined to comment to Reuters, citing court instructions.
High-powered attorney Daniel Kaiser quit from repping Rana in May. Yet another lawyer ceased repping the money man during negotiations with JPMorgan before the suit was filed.
Rana left JPMorgan in late 2025 for private equity firm Bregal Sagemount, which cut ties with him in April after less than six months on the job over performance concerns, company insiders previously told The Post.
The Post has sought comment from Norinsberg.

articles.title_orig: Discord Public Server Messages May Be Soon Searchable On Google, But You Can Opt Out
articles.title_zh: Discord Public Server Messages May Be Soon Searchable On Google, But You Can Opt Out
articles.content_orig:
The platform’s Discoverable Servers are about to get a lot more discoverable.
Discord is making a policy change that will further increase the visibility of conversations on its largest public servers. On November 16, the platform's Discoverable Servers will all be getting Server Web Pages. These hubs will display some basic information about the server, including a description and summaries of discussions happening on their public channels. By mid-December, Discord said that messages on posted to those channels could start appearing word-for-word on both the Server Web Pages and in search engine results. Neither the channel summaries nor the individual channel messages will display the poster's username or avatar.
The reason Discord gave for the change is to make it easier for information from these communities to be surfaced in web searches. In other words, you might start seeing Discord pages and messages the same way you'd find a Reddit thread among search hits.
This change is limited to Discoverable Servers, the large communities of at least 1,000 members where no invitation is required to join. Private servers, DMs and Group DMs will remain private. But considering Discord just weathered blowback over its implementation of age verification policies, this decision could raise new questions around how the platform handles privacy concerns.
Server admins for those Discoverable Servers can take action starting now to opt-out channels from being included in their eventual web presence. And individual users can also choose to keep their Discoverable Server posts from being indexed via the Data and Privacy section of Discord's User Settings. In select markets — the EU, UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia and South Korea — channel messages will be off by default to honor local regulations, so for those regions users will have to manually opt in to the feature. Teen Discord users are also excluded and do not have the option to turn on channel messages until they are of adult age.

articles.title_orig: China AI Hardware Firms Face Earnings Test After Stock Selloff
articles.title_zh: China AI Hardware Firms Face Earnings Test After Stock Selloff
articles.content_orig:
Lack of profits and the threat posed by western countries are raising concern about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boom
Trillions of dollars have been wiped from China’s stock markets in recent months amid increasing anxiety about the future of artificial intelligence, as Beijing races against the United States for dominance in the sector.
The STAR 50 Index, which tracks technology and innovation companies on the Shanghai stock exchange, has plunged 40% since June. Other indexes of major companies dropped by about 20% over the same time period.
The precipitous drop has wiped out $2.4tn from the Chinese stock market since May, according to Bloomberg.
AI stocks account for over 40% of the stock market value in China and Hong Kong, according to Goldman Sachs, meaning that any dent in value will send shockwaves across the whole domestic market.
The fall suggests that despite the government’s best efforts to boost China’s technology industries, particularly those which harness the power of AI, the domestic economy does not have the power to sustain a booming market.
The Chinese government has invested heavily into AI, including a 60bn yuan state-backed AI investment fund which started pumping money into domestic developers this month. But Chinese consumers have proved stubbornly reluctant to part with their cash in many parts of the economy – including technology – meaning that many tech companies struggle to turn a profit.
The lack of profits is one of several reasons for the sell-off. Another is the threat of western countries, especially the US, extending bans on Chinese technology.
“This year, the profit margin is not as good as expected. And the US is raising rates. And China’s domestic demand is so weak,” said Dan Wang, the China director for the Eurasia Group. She said that there was a “general anxiety” among technology companies about whether or not the state-backed model would work in the face of weak consumer demand.
The US has banned humanoid robots from China , citing national security risks, and is thought to be considering a ban on Chinese components in data centres. China is heavily reliant on exports and restrictions in the US hurt its domestic companies, which struggle to sell enough products at home.
As China races with the US to pull ahead in AI, Beijing has doubled down on robotics – also known as embodied AI – as the key to rolling out the technology across society. Robotics is also seen as the answer to China’s demographic problems, such as the ageing population and the shrinking workforce.
But the demand for robotics is being driven by government agencies and research institutions, rather than everyday consumers, for whom the products are still too expensive and not yet practical for home use. Humanoid robotics and robotic dogs have been popular in the entertainment industry but are yet to be useful in home settings.
Shares in Unitree, China’s leading robot-maker, have halved since they started trading in August.
“It doesn’t look like embodied intelligence could turn into profits in the in the mass market,” said Wang. Thin profit margins, rising rates in the US, and weak domestic demand were all contributing to a “general anxiety” among technology companies, she said.
China’s government wants local investors to invest their money domestically. China has in recent months restricted overseas investment, with more regulations taking effect from 1 December, but these moves have not led to greater investment in the Chinese markets.
Wang added that there was still optimism in other technology sectors, such as AI research and satellites, the latter because their links to the military indicates long term state support for the sector. And globally the AI boom is expected to last for at least another year.
On Monday, US AI company Anthropic, which makes the chatbot Claude, filed paperwork ahead of a planned IPO that could be the biggest stock market debuts of all time. The company is expected to bring in as much as $100bn.
China has no such blockbuster IPOs on the horizon. And despite pressure on policymakers to introduce stimulus measures to boost investment, none are expected to be announced during a politically sensitive period in China.
This week the top officials in the Chinese Communist party are gathering for the fifth plenum , an important meeting that will lay the groundwork for next year’s 21st Party Congress. The Congress is expected to anoint Xi Jinping, China’s leader, for a fourth term. There is no appetite for risky or potentially destabilising policy measures before then, even if there is a chance they could boost the economy.
Any stimulus measure would be “high risk”, Wang said. “What if it doesn’t work out? Then whoever came up with that policy, that guy would be held accountable”.

articles.title_orig: Two Nordic leaders urge Putin to end Ukraine war in rare direct contact by Europeans
articles.title_zh: Two Nordic leaders urge Putin to end Ukraine war in rare direct contact by Europeans
articles.content_orig:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said.
Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.
Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole.
"We've not set out to speak on behalf of anyone other than ourselves," Støre said.
Stubb added the call had been prepared in consultation with Ukraine and the US following a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Nordic leaders and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week.
The first trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks since the start of the year are tentatively planned for early November in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky later confirmed Stubb and Støre debriefed him after the call and said he was grateful for their "active support", while his Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been "the right approach".
Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the 90-minute call - held from Helsinki - to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.
Støre added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."
The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.
Putin also reaffirmed to the Nordic leaders what he views as the "root causes" of the conflict - his frequent shorthand for Ukraine's desire to exist as a sovereign state.
"A fair long-term peace settlement is possible only if Russia's legal interests are taken into account fully and unconditionally", Putin said.
All three parties reportedly agreed to continue their direct phone communication.
There was no official EU reaction to the talks. The dialogue had not been coordinated with other European leaders, the Danish and Swedish prime ministers said. "I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo," commented Sweden's Ulf Kristersson.
Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates was "moderately optimistic".
Relations between the US and Ukraine and its European allies have soured since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia, allowing Moscow to export oil to the America.
As the Trump administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to re-establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.
Stubb and Støre are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.
Soon after, Putin visited Alaska for a summit with Trump, and from then on Europeans were further sidelined from Ukraine peace talks. Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the EU of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.
But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".
And although he said Moscow did not view Finland and Norway as speaking on behalf of Europe, on Tuesday Peskov conceded that Stubb and Støre's talks with Putin had been "very constructive and practical talks with the leaders of two key neighbouring states."

articles.title_orig: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
articles.title_zh: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
articles.content_orig:
Inside Apple’s first folding iPhone, contact with the delicate inner screen could cause a stress ‘hotspot.’
Inside Apple’s first folding iPhone, contact with the delicate inner screen could cause a stress ‘hotspot.’
Within hours of the iPhone Duo launch last Friday, people reported that the inner screen on some brand new foldable phones was already broken. The issue was similar across many photos shared on social media: some kind of issue or crack would appear in the middle of the screen above the hinge, with lines appearing on the right side of the display. On Monday, Apple acknowledged an “issue” and said it’s replacing damaged units, without going into much detail about how many broken phones have been reported so far.
So what’s actually going on?
Shahram Mokhtari, the lead teardown technician at iFixit, has actually taken apart the iPhone Duo and has a pretty good idea about the potential cause, telling The Verge that it’s due to an issue along the hinge, where a series of gears, springs, and joints work together to let the device close flat, while also trying to avoid creating a deeper crease by giving that screen space to bend more gently inside while it’s closed.
At the troublesome spot, it appears that the flexible inner screen is pushing up against a part of the hinge. That inner screen is already “extremely sensitive,” he says — if you took a pick or a sharp tool and poked at the edges of the screen, “you’re going to break that screen.” If you look at the pictures of damaged Duos on social media, there’s often a black spot where the damage is focused on the display, and that’s where the metal is hitting the screen, Mokhtari says.
You can see a visual representation of what Mokhtari is talking about in iFixit’s written and video Duo teardowns, which reveal where the hinge transitions, as the center hinge support makes space for a crossing flex cable, creating several edges that could ultimately be the culprit. The damage iFixit has been seeing is at a point where the center support bar might not always drop down far enough while the screen folds, possibly creating a stress “hot spot” between the flat bar and the bent screen inside a closed iPhone Duo.
At least one user with a broken Duo screen said they “felt something around the internal hinge” while showing it to a friend, kept opening it, and heard an “audible crack,” with the screen breaking. YouTuber CuriousHagi, who covered a Duo with dirt as part of a strenuous durability test, captured something similar on video , and the screen break appears in a similar spot. In a teardown video, CuriousHagi found that a part of the hinge that connects to the central bar had snapped .
Apple says the issue affects a “small number” of Duo units, and Mokhtari says that “In terms of numbers, we don’t know. Apple definitely has all the data here. And I suspect they know more than they’re telling us as well.” But he notes that because foldable screens are so delicate, a “certain number” of them will fail, as will a number of the hinges because they’re also “extremely complicated and delicate.” And while Apple isn’t recalling the Duos, “If three months from now, we’re still seeing the same kind of failure, then it’s a more widespread problem, and that might lead to a recall,” Mokhtari says.
Mokhtari points out that since this is the first generation of the iPhone Duo, it’s the first time Apple’s engineers are getting data on the hinge, and he says that “I guarantee you” Apple will redesign what’s at fault here for its next-generation foldable. He also notes that, generally speaking, “the phones do seem to be in people’s hands and people are using them, and they’re not running into any issues whatsoever.”

articles.title_orig: Taylor Farms recalls salad kits sold at H-E-B. See affected product
articles.title_zh: Taylor Farms recalls salad kits sold at H-E-B. See affected product
articles.content_orig:
Taylor Farms, the produce giant linked to the nation's largest-ever cyclospora outbreak that sickened more than 20,000 people this summer, has issued a new salad recall .
Taylor Farms of Dallas is recalling Backyard BBQ Chop Salad kits sold at H-E-B stores because they may contain allergens not properly listed on its packaging, according to an Oct. 27 notice from the Food and Drug Administration.
The recalled kits contain undeclared soy and tree nuts (almonds) that could trigger reactions in people with sensitivities or allergies. No adverse reactions have been reported to date.
Taylor Farms has been a consistent fixture in headlines this year after health officials identified iceberg lettuce grown by Taylor Farms de Mexico as the source of an unprecedented outbreak of cyclosporiasis, a gastrointenstinal illness caused by the parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis. The FDA declared the outbreak over in September and said on Oct. 2 that it had concluded its investigation, which found cyclospora was present in the environment where the lettuce was grown and processed. This latest recall is not related to cyclospora or Taylor Farms de Mexico.
The recalled kits were distributed at H-E-B stores in Texas and are packaged in a plastic bag. The product's best-by date and UPC are on the back of the package.
H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad Kit 13.4-ounce; UPC 041220300457, best-by Oct. 30, 2026.
Do not consume the recalled salad kits; either dispose of them or return them to the place of purchase for a refund, per the FDA notice.
Customers with questions may contact Taylor Farms at 855-455-0098.

articles.title_orig: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
articles.title_zh: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
articles.content_orig:
Apple has announced refreshes for the iMac and the entry-level, 14-inch MacBook Pro . Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago.
The M6 is split into two variants for the iMac. Picking the “M6 chip with two Thunderbolt ports” option gets you a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, whereas picking “M6 chip with four Thunderbolt ports” gets you 12 cores for each, instead. The two-port variant maxes out at 24 GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, whereas the four-port one maxes out at 32GB of RAM and 2TB of storage.
There’s only one M6 chip option for the MacBook Pro—the one with the 12-core GPU and CPU. It caps out at 32GB of RAM, but can go to 4TB of storage.
It’s a more substantial refresh for the iMac, as its previous update introduced the M4. Apple  skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. In terms of performance gains moving from the M4 to the M6, Apple said with the Mac mini that users can expect up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, up to double graphics performance, and nearly five times faster on-device AI. All that largely matches what we saw when we tested the M6 Mac mini last month, and users of the new iMac should expect similar numbers.
The M6 iMac should see up to double SSD read/write performance compared to the M4 model, too.
The previous entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro had the M5, so that one is just stepping up a single generation. In this case, that means up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to double the Neural Engine performance.
In addition to the M6 chip, both computers now have the N1 chip for wireless connectivity (that means Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6). The iMac is now configurable with up to 2.5Gb Ethernet, while the MacBook Pro still lacks an Ethernet port.
There are no outward design changes to either device; they both look exactly the same as their immediate predecessors. The iMac starts at $1,499 for the two-port version, or $1,699 for the four-port version. The M6 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999.
Pre-orders start October 28, and they ship November 6.

articles.title_orig: Asian Stocks Set to Gain on Resurgent AI Optimism: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Asian Stocks Set to Gain on Resurgent AI Optimism: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
South Korea's KOSPI rose 4.53% from Monday's close to 5,717.30 on Tuesday morning. The jump made the Korea Exchange pause program buying for five minutes, its second brake in six days.
The first brake, on October 21, did not hold. The KOSPI gave back that entire rally within two sessions. For KOSPI holders, this rebound now rests on SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, which report results this week.
The Korea Exchange imposed the curb, known as a buy-side sidecar, at 10:13 a.m., Yonhap reported. Investor sentiment improved after artificial intelligence (AI) stocks rebounded in the US overnight.
Chip stocks led the US session on Monday. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index climbed 2.82%, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.82% to 26,169.38. The S&P 500 gained 0.70% to 7,676.77.
Brent crude also fell as Saudi, Pakistani, and Turkish officials held talks in Tehran. It traded at $114.64 a barrel early Tuesday, down 1.01% on the day. Even so, Brent remains 17.28% higher than a month ago.
Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens
Back in Seoul, Korea's memory giants led the move in Seoul. By 10:35 a.m., SK Hynix had climbed 7.14% to 1.366 million won. Samsung added 4.93% to 223,500 won.
Korea's gain outran Tuesday's moves elsewhere in Asia. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 1.96% to 63,407.69, and Taiwan's TAIEX added 0.47% to 46,260.03.
The gap ran the other way on October 15, when the KOSPI sank 7.57% after hot US inflation data. The Nikkei and TAIEX fell 4.90% and 3.41% that day. With so much weight in two memory makers, the KOSPI amplifies AI sentiment in both directions.
The rebound starts from a deep hole after weeks of chip-led selling. The KOSPI closed Monday nearly 40% under its June peak. Foreign investors sold a net 695.5 billion won that day.
Goldman Sachs cut its KOSPI target to 9,000 from 12,000 on Sunday. The bank says chip valuations imply a 65% fall in 2027 sector earnings, an outlook it calls overly negative.
SK Hynix reports third-quarter results on October 28, and Samsung follows on October 29. Memory chipmakers make up about half of the index.
Retail investors remain exposed to that outcome. Their 2026 net purchases carry an estimated average entry near 6,550, Global Markets Investor said. Tuesday morning's level sits about 13% below that.
Firm guidance on 2027 memory pricing would support Goldman's case. Weak outlooks would keep the 65% earnings-drop assumption priced in, and Tuesday's gains may then fade like the October 21 rally.

articles.title_orig: China’s top-secret spaceplane can’t hide in low-Earth orbit
articles.title_zh: China’s top-secret spaceplane can’t hide in low-Earth orbit
articles.content_orig:
A winged Chinese spacecraft bearing a strong resemblance to the US military’s X-37B spaceplane was photographed in orbit by a passing US-owned commercial satellite in 2024, and we finally have the image.
The Chinese spaceplane has delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module with power-generating solar arrays. In other words, the design of the winged ship is, to a great degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane flown by the US Space Force.
The photo was taken by a commercial imaging satellite owned by a company called Vantor, known as Maxar in 2024. Vantor is one of several companies that provide reconnaissance imagery of locations around the world to the US military and US intelligence agencies. The same Earth-imaging satellites can point their telescopes at objects in space.
Lower-resolution views of a Chinese spaceplane showing the vehicle’s general shape were publicly available before the DIA assessment. A US Space Force official revealed Maxar’s observation at a 2024 conference in South Korea, but the Pentagon did not release the full-resolution image to the public until Monday, when it appeared in an unclassified Defense Intelligence Agency assessment of threats to the United States in space.
The DIA report doesn’t reveal much new about what the Chinese spaceplane does in orbit. China has launched four spaceplane missions since 2020 with durations of up to nine months. The fourth mission is in orbit today after launching in February. It is not publicly known whether China has one or more such spaceplanes in its inventory.
The Space Force has two X-37Bs flying in rotation, with the longest of their eight missions to date running two-and-a-half years from launch until landing. US officials have released photos of the X-37B vehicles, published information about their design and dimensions, and disclosed a handful of experiments they have carried into orbit. Most of the X-37B’s activities in space are classified.
Like the X-37B, China’s spaceplane lifts off inside the payload shroud of a conventional rocket, then operates as a satellite once in orbit. The spaceplane flies like a miniature unpiloted version of NASA’s Space Shuttle and reenters the atmosphere for an autonomous land runway landing at the end of each mission. Ground teams then refurbish it for another flight.
The “enhanced maneuverability” of spaceplanes make them “more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites,” the DIA said in its report. So far, the Chinese spaceplane has only flown in low-Earth orbit (LEO) at an altitude of a few hundred miles. One of the Space Force’s X-37B flights soared to an altitude of more than 24,000 miles before using aerobraking to set up for reentry and landing .
Spaceplanes like China’s and the X-37B can also deploy small satellites from their cargo bay. Most recently, China demonstrated an ability to catch an object in orbit, perhaps using a robotic arm. The vehicle now in space released a sub-satellite in June and recaptured it in July, then did the same thing again in August and September, according to an analysis of open source orbital tracking data by Jonathan McDowell , an astrophysicist who catalogs spaceflight activity.
The official name of the Chinese spaceplane is even a mystery. It is often called Shenlong in Western publications, citing reports from the 2000s about China’s development of a robotic spaceplane. Chinese state media only refer to the vehicle as Chongfu Shiyong Shiyan Hangtian Qi, or CSSHQ, which means reusable experimental spacecraft, according to a fact sheet published by the Secure World Foundation .
The DIA did not disclose the exact circumstances of Maxar’s observation of the Chinese spaceplane, such as its timing, location, or distance, but Earth observations often use cameras to view other objects in space as their orbits intersect, an emerging field known as non-Earth imaging (NEI).
NEI allows commercial operators and government analysts to inspect satellites. This is especially useful for gleaning information about classified or proprietary satellite designs, extending a new avenue for international and corporate espionage to the high frontier.
The capability exhibited by Maxar and other commercial companies in the NEI field is distinct from the recent actions of some military spacecraft, such as Russia’s Kosmos 2612, which deliberately maneuvered to approach a US-registered radar imaging satellite earlier this month. Commercial NEI observations come from chance encounters, often at extremely high speed.
The DIA’s assessment of space threats includes an update on China’s pursuit of anti-satellite technology, or “counterspace” weapons. The intelligence agency reported the Chinese military likely considers directed-energy weapons (DEWs) “ideal counterspace systems” because they can be used to permanently or temporarily disable a satellite. One potential use for lasers in space would be to dazzle a sensor on an adversary’s satellite.
“China has multiple ground-based laser weapons with varying power levels to disrupt, degrade, or damage satellites in LEO,” the DIA said. “By the late 2020s, China may field space-based directed energy systems and higher-powered ground-based directed energy systems capable of threatening satellites in higher orbits.”
The DIA noted China’s testing of ground-based anti-satellite missiles and the country’s historic demonstration last year of satellite refueling in geosynchronous orbit, a regime some 22,000 miles (36,000 kilometers) over the equator, something no other country has achieved above LEO. China has also tested a robotic arm that could snag a spacecraft out of orbit, and now operates a growing fleet of satellites called TJS that routinely approach foreign spacecraft.
The US Space Force also has a constellation of inspector satellites in geosynchronous orbit and recently procured more that could be refueled, overcoming maneuverability limitations. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink revealed last month that the Pentagon has fielded weapons in space , making the United States the first nation to acknowledge possession of orbital weapons.
Russia is pursuing its own orbital combat program, which includes an ambition to deploy a nuclear weapon in space, according to US intelligence officials.
A more conventional Russian weapons system, known as Nivelir, is designed to fire projectiles from one satellite to smash into another. The Russian military simulated an attack using the Nivelir system in 2020. In April, Russia launched a fleet of small satellites into an orbit close to a commercial radar remote sensing satellite owned by ICEYE that provides reconnaissance imagery to Ukraine. One of the Russian satellites moved within “tens of meters” of the ICEYE satellite earlier this month before backing away, US officials said.

articles.title_orig: Apple Bets MacBook Pro Buyers Will Pay More for Touch Screens

articles.content_orig:
Apple introduces :br(s):the new 14‑inch :br(s):MacBook Pro with M6
Supercharged by M6, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features incredible performance and next-level AI capabilities, enhanced connectivity, and up to 24 hours of battery life, delivering even more value
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 , delivering even more performance, powerful on-device AI capabilities, and faster connectivity for college students, business users, creators, and more. M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. 1 The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power. 2 For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. 3 With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy. 4 In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere. 3 It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6.
“The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users — from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device,” said Shelly Goldberg, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With the powerful M6 chip, we’re taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value.”
M6: Blazing-Fast Performance and On-Device AI Capabilities
M6 brings even more performance and next-level AI capabilities to the 14-inch MacBook Pro. Featuring a powerful 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and faster unified memory, MacBook Pro with M6 is faster and more responsive.
The 12-core CPU, with two more cores than before, brings blazing-fast single- and multithreaded performance, so users can fly through everything from multitasking across apps to compiling code to handling complex creative workflows. The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5. 2 Everything from 3D modeling to photo editing and gaming feels incredibly fast, enhanced by a third-generation ray-tracing engine and Dynamic Caching to optimize on-chip memory. It also brings up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads, like LLM prompt processing, compared to M5. 3 The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 1.9x faster performance than M5 and works with the advanced GPU to dramatically accelerate AI workloads like image generation, Super Resolution, and AI upscaling. 2 The Neural Engine also powers Apple Intelligence, enabling advanced and energy-efficient on-device AI processing. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 does all this with industry-leading performance per watt and up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. With 16GB of unified memory standard, configurable up to 32GB, and higher memory bandwidth up to 170GB/s, MacBook Pro makes multitasking and working with demanding apps and large projects even faster.
The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 enables : 3
A Huge Upgrade with Even More Value
There’s never been a better time for customers to upgrade from a previous-generation MacBook Pro with Apple silicon or an Intel-based Mac. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers remarkable value thanks to major performance improvements and powerful AI capabilities. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro also features all of the compelling capabilities that have made it so popular, including:
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the Environment
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled.

Seagate (STX) dropped 30% in a month yet posted record Q4 revenue of $3.63B, up 48%, with supply allocated into 2028.
Morgan Stanley made a bullish case for battered Seagate and Western Digital (WDC) shares, according to Barron's.
Seagate trades at 18x forward earnings versus Western Digital's 23x, despite nearly identical operating margins of roughly 43%.

Seagate Technology ( NASDAQ:STX ) closed at $642.14. The 24/7 Wall St. price target is $794.02, which means 23.65% upside over the next 12 months. The stock gets a buy rating with 90% confidence, which counts as high conviction.
24/7 Wall St. Price Target
On the July call, CEO Dave Mosley said "data center demand now represents approximately 90% of our exabyte shipments" and that most nearline exabytes are "allocated into calendar 2028." The selloff prices in a cycle peak that Seagate's contracts don't yet show.
Shares fell 7.86% on October 22, 7.05% over the week and 30.13% over the past month. They are still up 133.96% year to date. The stock sits 43.8% below its 52-week high of $1,143.27 and about 197% above its low of $216.39. This week, Morgan Stanley ( NYSE:MS ) made a bullish case for battered Seagate and Western Digital ( NASDAQ:WDC ) shares, according to Barron's.
Fundamentals improved: fiscal Q4 revenue reached $3.63B, up 48.5% and ahead of the $3.49B consensus. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $5.71 against a $5.09 estimate, the fourth straight beat.
Free Report, Just Released

24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now . Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
And STX didn't make the cut!
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.

Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 52.7% from 37.9%. For fiscal Q1, management guided to revenue of $4.10B ± $100M and EPS of $7.30 ± $0.20.
HAMR technology is the growth engine. Exiting fiscal 2026, HAMR products made up about 40% of Seagate's nearline exabyte run rate. Mozaic 4, which supports up to 44 terabytes per drive, is scaling up with the two largest cloud providers. Mozaic 5 is on track for qualification shipments in late calendar 2027.
Because each disk holds more data, profit grows without adding factory output. Management said incremental gross margin is "well above the 60% figure." Agentic AI could add more demand as KV cache data spills onto hard drives, and so could physical AI, though Mosley called both "very early days."
Wall Street mostly agrees: 4 Strong Buys, 18 Buys, 2 Holds and 1 Strong Sell. The bull case hits $1,201.97, an 87.18% gain.
Hard drives have a long history of boom-and-bust cycles, and Seagate depends heavily on a small group of hyperscalers whose capex plans drive the whole order book (we profiled seven of the non-chip suppliers riding that same expansion, from power to cooling to storage, in a free report).
Other risks include dilution from the Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2028, tariffs, exposure to the Middle East conflict and settlement payments to the Commerce Department's BIS. Still, contracts set product configuration and pricing for all of calendar 2027, and Seagate paid down $1.40B of debt. The bear case sits at $614.24, a decline of just 4.34%.
Western Digital is the other half of the HDD duopoly. In fiscal Q1, its revenue grew 55.46% and non-GAAP gross margin hits 58.1%. It trades near 23x forward earnings, compared with our about 18x for Seagate.
Micron Technology ( NASDAQ:MU ) gives a memory-side contrast. At about 7x forward earnings, it shows how cheaply the market prices AI hardware it views as cyclical.
Seagate's margins are almost the same as Western Digital's, yet it trades at a lower multiple. That makes the 24/7 Wall St. price target look reasonable, and arguably conservative.
The 24/7 Wall St. price target of $794.02 carries a buy rating and 90% confidence. The critical factor is supply that is already allocated into 2028.
The thesis improved if fiscal Q1 results land near guidance and Mozaic 4 hits its milestones. It weakens if hyperscalers start shortening their planning horizons. Those are the signals to watch from here.
24/7 Wall St. Price Target
The outlook depends on Seagate keeping its HAMR roadmap on track. A sharp cut in hyperscaler capex is the biggest downside risk, while demand from agentic and physical AI is the biggest source of upside.
